    #22008. Tech Report: U.S. Trio Make First Snowboard and Ski Descent of a Near-7,000'er in Langtang

    📅 28 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1115 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Explorersweb ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: U.S. Trio Make First Snowboard and Ski Descent of a Near-7,000'er in Langtang

    📅 28 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1115 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • American snowboarder Nick Russell and skiers Adam Fabrikant and Billy Haas have just returned from Langtang with a first snowboard and ski descent of the south face of the formidable Dorje Lhakpa (6,966m).
    • The team climbed the peak, often known as the Langtang Pyramid, in two days in alpine style.
    • It has been revealed that on the summit of Dorje Lhakpa, October 30, 2026.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    American snowboarder Nick Russell and skiers Adam Fabrikant and Billy Haas have just returned from Langtang with a first snowboard and ski descent of the south face of the formidable Dorje Lhakpa (6,966m).

    The team climbed the peak, often known as the Langtang Pyramid, in two days in alpine style. They summited on October 20 and rode/skied down via the same line on the south face, while American photographer Blake Gordon and Canadian cinematographer Leo Hoorn filmed from a high camp.

    It has been revealed that on the summit of Dorje Lhakpa, October 30, 2026. Photo: Nick Russell.

    “The south face of Dorje was always the goal, and I’d been planning/dreaming of it for over two years,” Nick Russell told ExplorersWeb while on his way to the airport.

    According to recent reports, the expedition reached base camp on October 6, shortly after an intense storm blanketed Nepal’s mountains with heavy snow. For them, however, the snow was a blessing rather than a curse.

    “The cyclone gave our zone some much-needed snow down low, and on the face, it allowed a clean descent (no down climbing, no rappels),” Russell said.

    It has been revealed that sickness slowed the beginning of the expedition. “Three out of five of us, myself included, caught COVID,” Russell remarked. Luckily, the climbers recovered just as the weather cleared and winds dropped, followed by a string of perfect days.

    After the descent. Photo: Nick Russell/Instgram.

    In a recent development, “Adam, Billy, and I all carried our own gear, set the tracks, and climbed in alpine style on the face,” Nick Russell remarked. The team had hired three Sherpa climbers (Dawa Geljee Sherpa, Kami Sherpa, and Nuri Sherpa) who helped the camera crew get their gear to a high camp, plus a base camp crew, outfitted by Shangri-La Nepal Trek.

    Sources indicate that high camp at 6,000m on the south face of Dorje Lhakpa. Photo: Nick Russell/Instagram.

    The line of ascent/descent followed the snow from below 4,500m to Camp 1 (4,900m) by crossing an icefall. According to the team, this was the only real crux of the ascent, due to overhead serac hazard. At least, the exposed section was short — less than an hour.

    Recent findings suggest that on the first day of the summit push, the team continued to their high camp at 6,000m, below the col and at the base of the snowy face. Russell recalls the details of the climb as follows:.

    The south face is quite steep and sustained above the bergshrund, with sustained 45-50˚ and pockets of 55º, we estimate. The face had seen so much sun [over] the past two weeks that the rising conditions were the biggest unknown of the entire project.

    Industry observers note that we didn’t know whether or not it would be too icy to ride/ski until we got on the face. The snow was mostly firm, pretty much on the brink of being edge-able. It was two tool and crampon climbing the entire way, with no proper rests to take the pack off.

    According to recent reports, it took about 7.5 hours to climb the face, and we topped out around 1:30 pm. It took roughly 1.5 hours to descend, with breaks for the cameras to reset.

    According to recent reports, A climber leaves almost no tracks in the hard snow on Dorje Lhakpa. Photo: Nick Russell/Instagram.

    The three summiters started down from the top at the same time, Russell on snowboard and his partners on skis. It was anything but easy.

    Recent findings suggest that “The snow was more firm than I would have liked, but just edgeable enough to hold an edge,” Russell recalls. “Between the altitude, exposure below, steepness, and how firm it was, it was by far the heaviest line I’ve ever ridden.” He added that if the snow had been a little harder, they would have had to rappel down.

    Sources indicate that the hard snow on the upper sections. Photo: Nick Russell/Instagram.

    “You always hope for stable, boot-top powder, but that’s rarely the case at high altitude,” Russell explained. “Instead, you make the most of the conditions presented and try to do it as safely as possible.”.

    According to recent reports, he added: “The entire line was a no-fall zone; one lost edge, and it’d be over. Regardless of conditions, it was a dream for all of us to ride off the top of a peak in Nepal.”.

    After a partial descent, the team spent the night at high camp, hoping to ride some interesting slopes they had spotted earlier, but finally decided to bail the next morning. “We were satisfied,” Russell said. They continued on skis/snowboard all the way down to the moraines below Camp 1 around 4,500m.

    In a recent development, childhood friends Fabrikant and Haas often partner up on major ski expeditions, mainly in Alaska but also in the Himalaya. They climbed and skied both Gasherbrums 1 and 2 without oxygen after climbing them in the same style in 2024, together with Brendan O’Neill.

    “They are the strongest partners I’ve ever been in the mountains with,” said Russell, who has also climbed and snowboarded twice in the Indian Himalaya and twice in Nepal.

    “I tried Dhaulagiri in 2022 with Blake Gordon and Dan Corn, but the difficult conditions that year coupled with the loss of Hilaree Nelson [who fell to her death while trying to ski down Manaslu] didn’t allow us to make very much progress,” Russell noted.

    “I’ve always dreamed of riding lines in the Himalaya, and this felt like a major step forward in my personal journey,” he concluded.

    While this is the first ski and snowboard descent of Dorje Lhakpa’s south face, the legendary Marco Siffredi snowboarded the west ridge of the mountain in 1999, with Bertrand Delapierre. Siffredi perished shortly afterward on the Hornbein Couloir on Mount Everest. “Dorje Lhakpa first entered my psyche from Marco and Bertrand’s descent,” the rider recalled.

    The south face of Dorje Lhakpa was only climbed for the first time in 2021, by Spaniards Mikel Inoriza, Iker Madoz, and Mikel Zabalza.

    “I came across a photo of the south face and the American Alpine Journal article from the Spanish team’s first ascent in 2021,” Russell said. “The massive south face is visible from the Kathmandu Valley on a clear day, and it is honestly crazy to me that no one had skied it before.”.

    “Today,” he went on, “people are so hyper-focused on the 8,000m peaks (for good reason, I get it), but there are still virgin lines waiting for a snowboard/ski descent in the 6,000-7,000m range. It just takes a shit ton of work to make it happen.”.

    #22007. Tech Report: Saddle to Paddle: Bikerafting From Canada to Mexico

    📅 28 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (556 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Explorersweb ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Saddle to Paddle: Bikerafting From Canada to Mexico

    📅 28 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (556 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Pete Streufert and his friend Carter (no last name) are cycling 4,025km and packrafting 645km across the U.S.
    • According to recent reports, their route connects the rivers with long-distance cycling trails.
    • In a recent development, before starting the journey on September 17, he said they could find no record of anyone using this particular combination of rivers and cycling routes.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Pete Streufert and his friend Carter (no last name) are cycling 4,025km and packrafting 645km across the U.S. from Canada to Mexico. Starting in Glacier National Park, they will cross four rivers and six U.S. states to finish in El Paso, Texas.

    According to recent reports, their route connects the rivers with long-distance cycling trails. This allows the pair to cross landscapes that would usually require separate trips by bike and watercraft. Streufert, a geospatial wildfire scientist and cartographer, came up with the route by combining existing GPS tracks and geographical data from Bikepacking.com, American Whitewater, and OpenStreetMap. He overlaid cycling corridors and rivers to identify where the two could connect.

    In a recent development, before starting the journey on September 17, he said they could find no record of anyone using this particular combination of rivers and cycling routes. So it is possible that they are the first to do so.

    They started what they neatly call the Saddle to Paddle Traverse on September 17, from Glacier National Park, Montana, on the Canadian border. They kicked off the first packrafting section with a 115km descent of the North Fork of the Flathead River, which forms part of the western boundary of Glacier National Park.

    Sources indicate that from there, they followed the Great Divide Mountain Bike Route through Montana toward Jackson Lake, Wyoming, for 1,107km. Here, they hit their second paddling phase on the Snake River.

    Every time they reach a river, the pair inflates their rafts, load their bicycles aboard, and paddle downstream. Then at each takeout, they deflate the rafts, attach them to their bikes, and continue riding.

    Industry observers note that the route. Photo: Pete Streufert.

    Sources indicate that after 130km along the Snake River, their route joined the SLoToJa cycling corridor. They pedaled through Idaho, Wyoming, and Utah. Here, a short connector track took them onto the newly developed Golden Gravel Trail. A further 860km of cycling brought them to Utah’s Green River.

    They then paddled 328km through Desolation and Gray Canyons, including a handful of Class III rapids, and their only Class IV rapid of the trip.

    It has been revealed that pulling their rafts out in Canyonlands National Park, they took the White Rim Trail to Moab. They are now taking a few days in Moab to “get all the mud off our bikes and escape the rain for a day or two before we keep heading south,” states Streufert.

    From here, they will once again pick up the Golden Gravel Trail through the La Sal Mountains and across Colorado, then continue on the Great Divide Mountain Bike Route to New Mexico.

    Paddling the Green River. Photo: Pete Streufert.

    A final paddling section on Latest Mexico’s Rio Chama will take them to the last leg of the trip, a 950km ride to El Paso.

    Industry observers note that the pair are riding Rodeo Labs Flaanimal 6.0 Steel, fitted with 29-inch Vittoria Mezcal tires, and using Kokopelli packrafts. The pair have described this as a “self-supported” route, although of course they’re replenishing their food along the way. They seem to combine camping with staying in towns.

    View this post on Instagram See this post on Instagram.

    They should complete the journey within the next few weeks, within their two-month timeline. You can follow their progress here.

    Latest Update: Buying a Duplex? Live in One Side to Put as Little as 3.5% Down

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (509 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Moneycrashers

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, lenders treat a duplex you live in as your home, so you can finance it with as little as 3.5% down on a government-insured FHA loan or 5% on a conventional loan.
    • Recent findings suggest that buy the same duplex as a rental you won’t live in, and an FHA loan, which the Federal Housing Administration insures, is off the table.
    • Recent findings suggest that FHA’s 3.5% minimum needs a credit score of 580 or higher, and scores from 500 to 579 need 10% down.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, lenders treat a duplex you live in as your home, so you can finance it with as little as 3.5% down on a government-insured FHA loan or 5% on a conventional loan. Buy one only if the other side’s rent, minus a quarter for repairs and empty months, leaves you paying less than a similar apartment rents for.

    Recent findings suggest that buy the same duplex as a rental you won’t live in, and an FHA loan, which the Federal Housing Administration insures, is off the table. A conventional loan, one without government insurance, then takes 25% down.

    Recent findings suggest that FHA’s 3.5% minimum needs a credit score of 580 or higher, and scores from 500 to 579 need 10% down. Freddie Mac, which buys many conventional loans from lenders, allows 5% down when its automated system approves the loan and the loan stays within a standard size limit, and 15% otherwise. Both loans require you to move in within 60 days and live there at least a year, after which you can move out and rent both sides.

    Either way, the lender counts 75% of the rent the other side is expected to bring when it decides whether you can afford the payment. Fannie Mae, the other big buyer, counts it only if you already pay rent or own a home.

    It has been revealed that say you put $12,600, or 3.5%, down on a $360,000 duplex, and your full payment, with taxes and insurance that covers the rented side, is $3,000 a month. The other side rents for $1,900, and a similar apartment would rent for $2,000. The tenant’s rent leaves you $1,100 to pay. Set aside a quarter of that rent, $475, for repairs and months the unit sits empty, and your side costs $1,575, or $425 less than the $2,000 apartment. A gap like that makes the duplex worth buying if you’re ready to live next to your tenant.

    It has been revealed that you’ll likely share a yard with your tenant, screen applicants, and take repair calls yourself. A duplex also draws fewer buyers than a single-family home when you sell. If those trade-offs outweigh the savings, there are other ways to cut your housing cost by renting out part of your home, from a spare room to a basement unit.

    Get two numbers before you bid: what similar units nearby rent for, from current listings, and your full monthly payment, from a lender’s quote.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that the federal tax credits that covered up to 30% of the cost of insulation, heat pumps, windows, and home solar ended for work installed after 2025. Before you sign a contract, check what your utility and your state will pay, since many rebates pay only if you apply first or use an approved contractor.

    Sources indicate that the IRS ties the credits to the year the work was installed, not the year you paid, so a heat pump paid for in December 2025 and installed in January earns no credit. Work installed by the end of 2025 still counts, and if your 2025 return left it out, you can claim it on an amended return with Form 5695 within three years of when you filed.

    Many utilities still pay rebates on heat pumps and insulation, and some states offer their own tax credits. Some state energy offices also run one or both federally funded Home Energy Rebates programs. One pays up to $4,000 toward a whole-home upgrade at any income, and more to lower-income households. The other pays up to $14,000 for electric upgrades like heat pumps to households earning up to 150% of their area’s median income, though no longer to replace gas or oil equipment.

    Industry observers note that the federal credits came at tax time, after the job. A rebate program may need to approve your project and your contractor before the work begins, and it pays only for equipment that meets its efficiency rules.

    Search your ZIP code on DSIRE, NC State University’s database of state and utility incentives, and on ENERGY STAR’s Rebate Finder. Then check your utility’s rebates page, and ask your state energy office whether its programs have opened. A home energy audit from your utility can also point you to rebates.

    It has been revealed that redo the payback, the years an upgrade’s savings take to cover its cost, counting only rebates you’ve confirmed. Say your utility’s rebate is the same as in 2025, a heat pump would have earned the full $2,000 credit, and it cuts your bills by $500 a year. It now costs you $2,000 more than it would have in 2025, which adds four years to its payback. That extra cost can put the cheap upgrades that pay back fastest ahead of big projects.

    Before you sign, ask the contractor which of these programs it’s enrolled in, and get any approval a rebate requires in writing.

    The 101 money moves that matter most, from the foundations to protecting what you’ve built.

    Latest Update: Your 401k Contribution Limit Resets Every January – Max It If You Can

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (482 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, your 401(k) contribution limit starts over on January 1, and any room you don’t use by your last December paycheck is gone for good.
    • Recent findings suggest that doing this every January matters because the limit moves.
    • It has been revealed that the limit counts contributions by calendar year, and every dollar has to come out of that year’s paychecks.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, your 401(k) contribution limit starts over on January 1, and any room you don’t use by your last December paycheck is gone for good. Each January, look up the fresh IRS limit, divide it by your number of paychecks, and set your contribution to that amount if your budget allows.

    Recent findings suggest that doing this every January matters because the limit moves. The IRS adjusts it for inflation, and when it rises, a per-paycheck amount that maxed you out last year leaves room unused.

    It has been revealed that the limit counts contributions by calendar year, and every dollar has to come out of that year’s paychecks. It’s also a limit per person, not per job. If you switched employers this year, what went into the old blueprint counts too, and keeping the combined total under the limit is on you.

    It has been revealed that to hit the max from any point in the year, take the current limit, subtract what you’ve already contributed, and divide by the paychecks you have left. Enter that as a dollar amount, or convert it to a percentage of your pay. If you’ll be 50 or older by December 31 and your proposal offers catch-up contributions, you can add one on top, with a larger allowance in the years you turn 60 through 63. In a plan with a Roth option, the IRS requires the catch-up to go in as Roth, taxed now instead of at withdrawal, if your wages from that employer topped the high-earner threshold the year before.

    Spread your contributions across the whole year if your employer matches each paycheck. Hit the limit by summer and the later paychecks can go unmatched, unless your plan makes up the difference with a year-end true-up. Ask HR which kind you have.

    If you changed jobs, add up both looks before you set the new rate. Any excess has to come out by April 15 of the following year, or it’s taxed twice, once for the year you contributed it and again when you withdraw it.

    Recent findings suggest that contribute at least enough to collect your whole employer match if the full limit is out of reach. Then put part of every pay raise toward a higher rate. Your take-home pay still grows, and contributions that rise faster than the limit shrink the gap to the max.

    Solo Trekker Flouts Khumbu Rules, Evacuated After Cliff Fall

    📅 28 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (270 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Explorersweb

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that A 26-year-old Australian solo trekker who fell from a cliff near Lobuche in the Everest region has been evacuated by helicopter to Kathmandu.
    • It has been revealed that joshua Patrick Cherubino sustained severe head injuries after falling at Kongma La Pass.
    • Kongma La, at about 5,535m, is the highest of the trio of high passes on the classic Everest Three Passes circuit.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that A 26-year-old Australian solo trekker who fell from a cliff near Lobuche in the Everest region has been evacuated by helicopter to Kathmandu. He is recovering in intensive care. By law, all foreign trekkers are supposed to have a guide in the Khumbu.

    It has been revealed that joshua Patrick Cherubino sustained severe head injuries after falling at Kongma La Pass. He was first taken to Lobuche, then flown out on October 27, according to The Tourism Times.

    Kongma La, at about 5,535m, is the highest of the trio of high passes on the classic Everest Three Passes circuit. It links the Chhukung side of the Imja Valley with Lobuche over rocky, non-glaciated moraine. The crossing is long and remote; the descent toward Lobuche is often loose underfoot and comes after hours already spent at altitude.

    The case has again drawn attention to Nepal’s rules in the Khumbu. Since 2023, the Nepal Tourism Board has required that all foreign trekkers be accompanied by a licensed guide within national parks, including Sagarmatha.

    In practice, the local Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality has continued to matter its own permits and has not strictly enforced the national guide requirement. Thus, independent trekking remains common on the main Everest routes. Officials quoted by The Tourism Times described unguided travel in the region as a violation of the mandatory rule and a source of preventable rescues.

    Cherubino was traveling alone when he was found. No further details on the circumstances of the fall or his condition have been released beyond the hospital’s assessment that he is recovering.

    #21997. Breaking: The Hidden Benefit Of Being Retired In A Bear Market

    📅 06 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1982 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Financialsamurai ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: The Hidden Benefit Of Being Retired In A Bear Market

    📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1982 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Financialsamurai

    ⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that as my public equity portfolio gets obliterated thanks to being overweight tech stocks, I started dusting off my resume to go back to flipping burgers at McDonald’s.
    • As every long-time investor knows, the name of the game is survival.
    • It has been revealed that we're not in an official bear market, yet.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that as my public equity portfolio gets obliterated thanks to being overweight tech stocks, I started dusting off my resume to go back to flipping burgers at McDonald’s. Then halfway through the application, I wiped away my tears and took a deep breath.

    As every long-time investor knows, the name of the game is survival. If you can make it through the downturn, good things usually await on the other side.

    It has been revealed that we're not in an official bear market, yet. But plenty of individual tech names have already fallen by over 20%, and when you're overweight those names, the index's official status doesn't matter much.

    So I thought it might be helpful for those who are retired, or who are close, to discuss the positives of going through a downturn. We'll also review how long downturns usually last so we can better prepare.

    Sources indicate that as the midterm elections highlighted, a lot of people are not happy with the way our country has been led. But the discontent didn't appear overnight. The stock market was simply acting as a giant dose of Lidocaine.

    Industry observers note that as long as stocks kept going up, we could more easily bear higher oil prices, higher food prices, higher housing costs, higher college tuition costs, and explosive medical costs. After all, our investment returns were growing faster than inflation. $6 for a gallon of gas stings a lot less when your brokerage account is up $50,000 for the year.

    But that tolerance for rising costs disappears the moment our investments start losing money. Suddenly, $89 a pound for wagyu feels personal.

    According to recent reports, when the wealth effect vanishes, consumers cut back. Fewer dinners out. Fewer vacations. The upcoming car gets pushed out another year. With declining corporate profitability, companies accelerate layoffs to protect margins. The newly unemployed tighten spending even further.

    Rinse and repeat until economists officially declare a recession six months after everybody already felt it.

    In a recent development, if you see the writing on the wall, you want want to get ahead of the layoffs by negotiating your own severance package. If you do, you will probably have an easier time getting a much better exit offer than being lumped with the masses.

    Industry observers note that if you're newly retired, your biggest fear is sequence of returns risk. That's the risk of suffering big losses early in retirement while you're also withdrawing money to live on. Do that for too long and your portfolio may never recover.

    Lose enough and you get forced back to work. Nobody who has tasted freedom wants to return to Monday morning status meetings and performance reviews from someone half their age.

    Retirees who live off their investments should feel worse about a bear market more than the average worker. We don’t have a paycheck to cushion the blow. We may not have much spare cash flow to buy the dip either.

    It has been revealed that but here's the key point. If your investments can survive the correction or bear market, you should actually feel good during a downturn. Not ecstatic, but relatively good. Because the alternative is working hard for no financial reward.

    How do you know if you can survive? Run through this quick checklist:.

    So how long will the pain last? History offers some comfort, provided you have the patience of a parent waiting for a toddler to put on his shoes while already 15 minutes late.

    According to recent reports, according to Capital Group, the S&P 500 has dropped 10% or more about once every 18 months since 1954. A 20%+ bear market shows up about once every six years.

    According to recent reports, in other words, if you strategy on a 40-year retirement, expect roughly 25 corrections and six or seven bear markets. Declines are the price of admission, not a sign the world is ending. Get used to them.

    Source: Capital Group, S&P 500 data from 1954 through 2025.

    Sources indicate that hartford Funds, using Ned Davis Research data going back to 1928, counts 27 bear markets. Stocks fell 35% on average and took 289 days, or about 9.6 months, to hit bottom.

    In a recent development, bear markets were far more common during the Depression era. Since 1945, there have been 15, or one about every 5.1 years.

    Two caveats before you get too comfortable. First, these figures measure peak to trough. Getting back to your old high takes longer. Second, the 1973 and 1980 bear markets each dragged on for more than 600 days. Averages are nice until you're living through the outlier.

    It has been revealed that but here's the part that should make everyone feel better. Every S&P 500 correction since 1929 has been followed by a recovery, and the average return in the first year after the bottom was 52%. And the recoveries are happening quicker now, if we include the 2025 Liberation Day and 2026 Iran War events.

    Hartford also found that about 42% of the S&P 500's strongest days over the past 20 years occurred during bear markets. Sell in a panic and you'll likely miss the rebound.

    My takeaway: In a realistic worst-case scenario, blueprint on gutting out roughly 12 to 18 months of pain from peak to trough, with a longer tail to fully recover. That's why the one to two years of cash is fine, especially with interest rates still high.

    The existential dilemma of a bear market is this:.

    The correct answer is to work less hard and YOLO more. Let me explain using a concept I call Return On Effort (ROE).

    During a bull market, working less hard actually increases your Return On Effort because your investments provide most of the returns. Unless you have a sales job or some other role tightly correlated to performance, an extra 15 hours a week rarely moves the needle. You're better off riding the organization's growth.

    During a bear market, working hard to run in place or lose money makes even less sense. There's nothing you can do to stem declining consumer confidence, upcoming socialist policies, higher taxes, and so forth. Your boss isn't handing out raises while revenue is falling. See Google's collapse after having such a huge lead in the AI race.

    If anything, your extra effort earns you the privilege of doing the work of three colleagues who just got laid off. Congratulations on your 0% raise.

    According to recent reports, so you work less hard to protect your declining Return On Effort. Not because you're lazy. Because you're rational.

    In a recent development, with this logic in mind, who works the least? The unemployed, the traditional retiree, and the early retiree.

    Sources indicate that therefore, so long as your investments can withstand the beating, you're going to be just fine. Psychologically, as a retiree, you must push yourself to do less and have more fun.

    According to recent reports, happiness is relative. During a bull market, plenty of early retirees feel a twinge of FOMO watching former colleagues get promoted and cash fat RSU checks. During a bear market, that FOMO flips. Nobody envies the guy grinding through a reorg while his stock comp gets cut in half.

    Whether you’re retired or still grinding away, a downturn offers some real perks.

    1) Things get cheaper. When demand falls, so do prices for travel, hotels, and eventually real estate. Retirees with flexible schedules can travel off-peak and score deals that working parents can only dream about. Workers looking to buy their first home may finally face less competition.

    According to recent reports, 2) You get to shop the sale. Retirees with passive income and a cash buffer get to buy when others are forced to sell. Workers get an even steadier advantage. Every paycheck and 401(k) contribution now picks up more shares at lower prices. Steady income plus a long time horizon makes you the natural buyer in a bear market.

    3) Your kids get to buy the dip. I’ve written about how to use stock market downturns to make your kids millionaires. As a father, this is my favorite benefit of a bear market. Because the equity train finally stops long enough for kids to catch up and hop on board. A child has 50+ years of compounding ahead. A 30% drop today is a rounding error by the time they’re in their 50s.

    4) Tax moves get better. Tax-loss harvesting offsets future gains. Roth conversions at depressed valuations mean you pay less tax on the same number of shares, and all the recovery happens tax-free.

    It has been revealed that 5) The AI hedge is doing its job. Public AI stocks have gotten crunched. But there’s a flip side. If AI companies are struggling to justify their valuations, AI probably isn’t wiping out white-collar work as fast as everyone feared. That’s comforting for our kids, and for every worker wondering if their job will exist in 10 years.

    Industry observers note that 6) You get humbled and build resilience. Being heavily overweight tech felt brilliant for years. Bear markets remind us we’re not as smart as we thought. My advice after every huge win is to go scrub all your toilets. Every downturn you survive makes you a calmer, better investor for the next one. If you’re still working, just make sure your emergency fund is solid, because layoffs tend to show up at the worst time.

    It has been revealed that you can’t control tech volatility, interest rates, or who wins elections. But you can control how you spend your time during a downturn.

    Recent findings suggest that the market will eventually recover. It always has. When it does, the people who grinded through the downturn will be exhausted. Those of us who leaned into family, friends, and fitness will be well rested. Both groups will survive, which is what matters most.

    Industry observers note that if you’ve been thinking about retiring, a bear market may be the best time to pull the trigger. It means that in spite of the carnage, your finances are strong enough for you to break free. Waiting for the next bull market can feel safer, but it’s backwards.

    Sources indicate that if your finances can support retirement while stocks are down 20% or more, your strategy has already passed the stress test. You’re not retiring on inflated numbers that could vanish in the next correction. And since bear markets don’t last forever, a recovery may carry your retirement forward with a tailwind instead of a headwind.

    According to recent reports, compare that to the person who retires at the peak of a bull market, only to watch their portfolio drop 30% in the first two years. That’s sequence of returns risk at its worst.

    So go play in the park. Take your kids to the beach. A downturn is the best time to enjoy the freedom you worked so hard to build, and maybe the best time to claim it.

    Are you finding it more comforting to be retired during a downturn, or more stressful? How much of your portfolio would need to fall before you'd seriously consider going back to work? Do you agree that working less hard in a bear market is the rational move, or is that just a cop-out for the lazy? And for those still working, has the market selloff made you rethink how hard you're grinding? Are you using the downturn to fund your kids' investment accounts?

    Industry observers note that if you want a roadmap for getting through downturns and coming out richer, pick up a copy of Millionaire Milestones: Simple Steps To Seven Figures, a USA Today bestseller. It covers how to keep investing when everybody else is scared, so you can reach financial independence sooner.

    #21995. West Ridge or Hornbein Couloir? Everest Team Prepares for Fourth Attempt

    📅 29 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (633 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Explorersweb ↗ Open Full Page

    West Ridge or Hornbein Couloir? Everest Team Prepares for Fourth Attempt

    📅 29 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (633 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Russian team is preparing to head up Everest’s West Ridge for a fourth time.
    • Sources indicate that andrei Vasiliev, Vitaly Shipilov, and Sergey Kondrashkin are in Kathmandu recovering from a viral infection and waiting out Cyclone Arnab, which is now weakening.
    • Sources indicate that everest West Ridge some days ago.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Russian team is preparing to head up Everest’s West Ridge for a fourth time. While no easy option exists, they want to avoid the extremely exposed, difficult, and uncertain ridge route. Their only alternative is the Hornbein Couloir, which would force them to stray temporarily into Tibet.

    Sources indicate that andrei Vasiliev, Vitaly Shipilov, and Sergey Kondrashkin are in Kathmandu recovering from a viral infection and waiting out Cyclone Arnab, which is now weakening. They will return to their base in Lobuche this weekend, determined to climb Everest without supplemental oxygen.

    Sources indicate that everest West Ridge some days ago. Photo: Andrei Vasiliev.

    “So far, we have completed three rotations on the mountain,” leader Vasiliev told ExplorersWeb. “Part of this time was spent exploring different options for accessing the route.”.

    The Russian team has a permit to climb Everest from Nepal, as long as they attempt a route other than the standard Khumbu Icefall-South Col-Southeast Ridge. This has become the normal South Side route since Hillary and Tenzing’s first ascent in 1953.

    Topo of the Russian team’s planned route on Everest, courtesy of Andrei Vasiliev.

    First, the Russians tried to bypass the Khumbu Icefall via the Nuptse Shoulder toward Camp 1, but heavy snow forced them to find another route. Crossing the Icefall (sharing paths with the normal route) was also too hard in the deep snow and on the shaky snow bridges over the innumerable crevasses.

    Industry observers note that “Eventually, we selected a third option, via the Lho La,” Vasiliev remarked. “From that pass, our planned route continues across the West Shoulder, along the West Ridge.”.

    At the Lho La col. Photo: Andrei Vasiliev.

    In a recent development, on their latest foray, the team reached 6,400m. “We climbed approximately twelve 60m pitches over rock, snow, and ice of moderate difficulty,” stated Vasiliev.

    He noted that on the way to the West Shoulder, they found traces of previous expeditions, including old ropes and snow anchors.

    As for the terrain ahead of them, Vasiliev stated:.

    Industry observers note that from our highest point reached, the terrain ahead looks manageable. We can see two more steep rock steps, each approximately 100m high, along with possible bypasses on steep snow slopes. Beyond these obstacles, the terrain appears easier, and we hope to be able to move simultaneously.

    Industry observers note that rocky section on the way to Everest’s West Ridge. Photo: Andrei Vasiliev.

    Vasiliev and his team are confident they can manage this route, despite doing so in increasingly wintry conditions.

    It has been revealed that the route linking the Lho La, the West Shoulder, and the West Ridge of Everest has been completed only twice. A Yugoslavian team led by Tone Skarja did the first complete ascent in 1979. They used the Hornbein Couloir variation on their descent.

    Recent findings suggest that the only repetition was done by a Bulgarian team in 1984. Hristo Prodanov reached the summit on his own and retraced his steps down the ridge but never made it back alive. Some of his partners who summited days later descended via the normal route. Three other teams who climbed the West Shoulder-West Ridge summited by traversing to the North Face, on the Chinese side, and climbing the Hornbein Couloir.

    In a recent development, the North Face of Everest from the West Shoulder. Photo: Andrei Vasiliev.

    According to recent reports, objectively speaking, the Hornbein Couloir offers more summit (and survival) chances than the upper part of the West Ridge. However, it requires traversing into Chinese territory. The Russian team has a permit to climb only from Nepal. It is unclear if a brief border trespass could be considered, and Vasiliev has not confirmed what they will do. “First we need to complete one more rotation,” he noted.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, since 1975, Nikon’s Small World competition has featured images produced by optical microscopes, an art that usually stays in scientific papers and textbooks.
    • In a recent development, the fruiting bodies of a Hemitrichia slime mold remind one distinctly of Dr.
    • Sources indicate that the winning image shows bubbling globules of black ink being injected onto a piece of paper by an inkjet printer.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, since 1975, Nikon’s Small World competition has featured images produced by optical microscopes, an art that usually stays in scientific papers and textbooks. But through the carefully engineered lenses of the microscope, photomicrographers sometimes capture glimpses of strikingly surreal, alien beauty. The 2026 Photomicrography Competition winners include subjects both living and mechanical, small and very small.

    In a recent development, the fruiting bodies of a Hemitrichia slime mold remind one distinctly of Dr. Seuss. Photo: Eric Epstein/Nikon Small World.

    Sources indicate that the winning image shows bubbling globules of black ink being injected onto a piece of paper by an inkjet printer. Behind the lens was 25-year-old German design student Ole Bielfeldt, whose work explores the surprising complexity of everyday objects. His process is largely DIY: Bielfeldt builds his own setups, cobbles together parts, and learns techniques online.

    “I just pick somewhere to start and go for it,” Bielfeldt explained. “You’re likely going to fail at first, and that’s what makes it even more interesting.”.

    The experimentation and imperfection, he added, are the most interesting parts of the process and, ultimately, more notable to him than achieving the highest image quality.

    Photo: Ole Bielfeldt/Nikon Small World.

    Ah, mice; the humble martyrs to scientific progress. A significant amount of science seems to involve cutting up mice and learning from the result. But in this sort of photography, even the strongest mouse advocate must admit that the results are visually spectacular.

    Satu Paavonsalo and Dr. Sinem Karaman of the University of Helsinki took this image of a mouse’s eye while researching drug therapy. Photo: Satu Paavonsalo and Dr. Sinem Karaman/Nikon Small World.

    Third place went to another rodent part: a 5X-magnified image of neurons in a mouse’s brain.

    Photo: Kaelin Wulf and Rachel Flannery/Nikon Small World.

    It has been revealed that in defense of humanity, we were also willing to subject our own body parts to photographic investigation. The 7th-place winner came from Dr. Bruno Cisterna and Dr. Eric Vitriol at the Medical College of Georgia at Augusta University. Using confocal imaging, which involves scanning a specimen to generate optical sections, they captured human neurons at 20X magnification.

    Industry observers note that these human neurons were grown from reprogrammed skin cells. Photo: Dr. Bruno Cisterna and Dr. Eric Vitriol/Nikon Small World.

    Sources indicate that I’ll end with a personal favorite of mine, John-Oliver Dum’s image of a little jumping spider, dusted with pollen. Dum, who won second place, credits a childhood bite for his fascination with spiders. The pollen was cultivated by his wife, specifically to create images like this one.

    Recent findings suggest that you can disagree, but I think this little guy is adorable. Photo: John-Oliver Dum.

    You can view the full gallery of winners and honorable mentions here. If you want to see photos of larger things, check out the winners from the Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026, Aerial Photography, 2026 Ocean Photographer of the Year, or Memorial Maria Luisa International Photo and Video competitions.

    College Students Found Dead After Hiking Colorado Mountain

    📅 29 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (505 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The two young men who set off into Colorado’s Sawatch Mountains this month were both passionate about taking the outdoors seriously.
    • Sources indicate that but both of them were found dead Wednesday, under circumstances that remain unclear.
    • The bodies were finally discovered near West Apostle Mountain on October 28, just outside of Gunnison, Colorado.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The two young men who set off into Colorado’s Sawatch Mountains this month were both passionate about taking the outdoors seriously. One was studying to be a wildland firefighter, while the other hoped to become a mountain guide.

    Sources indicate that but both of them were found dead Wednesday, under circumstances that remain unclear. Local authorities spent days looking for missing hikers Kaden Matsuda, 19, and Jackson Donlon, 20.

    The bodies were finally discovered near West Apostle Mountain on October 28, just outside of Gunnison, Colorado.

    Matsuda and Donlon, students at Colorado Mountain College in Leadville, had planned on hiking and camping near Ice Mountain, a 13,960-foot peak located about 50 miles from Gunnison.

    Recent findings suggest that they left for their trip on Oct. 23. College staff notified local authorities they were missing on Oct. 26, according to the Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office. The men’s families remarked they were both experienced hikers.

    Matsuda was studying to be a wildland firefighter, and Donlon was training to become a mountain guide.

    In a recent development, kaden Matsuda, left, and Jackson Donlon. Supplied: Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office.

    Kaden Matsuda, left, and Jackson Donlon. Supplied: Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office.

    Industry observers note that search-and-rescue teams were deployed and found their vehicle at the trailhead. Weather conditions looked risky, with heavy snow falling in Chaffee County.

    “Ice Mountain is a very technical climb, and it is recommended that hikers be very experienced when trying to tackle it. That is when it is dry. Although there was only about eight inches of snow around Kaden’s vehicle and in the lower basin, Ice Mountain received one to two feet of snow,” the sheriff’s office said in a Facebook post.

    In a recent development, multiple local SAR teams worked on the case. Photo: Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office.

    Multiple local SAR teams worked on the case. Photo: Chaffee County Sheriff’s Office.

    In a recent development, rescue teams used drones, helicopters, and dogs to search for the two hikers. On October 27, they located their tent, which had collapsed under the weight of the snow, near West Apostle Mountain (13,597 feet). Inside were sleeping bags, stoves, and other equipment, but the two men were nowhere to be found.

    The next day, authorities unveiled they had found their bodies in the mountain’s basin. Officials declined to share potential causes of death, beyond stating that they did not suspect foul play.

    Sources indicate that the Sawatch Range of the Rocky Mountains is home to many 13,000- and 14,000-foot peaks. Some of them, like West Apostle Mountain, require technical climbing ability and become substantially more difficult and dangerous during wet weather. The route up the mountain requires traversing fields of loose boulder scree and talus that can be hazardous after snow.

    From 2010 to 2017, eight people have died in the Sawatch Mountains. Falls are the most common cause of fatalities for those tackling Colorado’s 13ers and 14ers, as the state’s highest mountains are known to locals.

    #21989. Loud Wealth vs. Stealth Wealth: Why Materialism Fades Over Time

    📅 09 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1469 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Financialsamurai ↗ Open Full Page

    Loud Wealth vs. Stealth Wealth: Why Materialism Fades Over Time

    📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1469 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Financialsamurai

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that I’m a proponent of stealth wealth.
    • It has been revealed that stealth wealth is also the natural endgame of following FIRE principles for decades.
    • Industry observers note that so by default, every long-term FIRE practitioner eventually becomes a stealth wealth practitioner.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that I’m a proponent of stealth wealth. It makes for a more peaceful life with lower expectations and less scrutiny. The last thing you want to do is show off and put you and your family in danger.

    It has been revealed that stealth wealth is also the natural endgame of following FIRE principles for decades. If you keep living well below your means, which is required to retire early, your investments will eventually compound faster than you can spend.

    Industry observers note that so by default, every long-term FIRE practitioner eventually becomes a stealth wealth practitioner. Whether they mean to or not.

    Industry observers note that in private, you can do whatever you want. But in public, staying low-key is better. Here are three simple steps to follow:.

    Recent findings suggest that 1) Dress simply. No designer brands or fancy outfits. Clean, comfortable clothes are all you need. Think jeans, t-shirt, warm jacket, sweater, sneakers, baseball hat.

    2) Drive an old car. Driving a upcoming car is stressful and can attract unwanted attention. If you insist on a luxury brand, try to keep it for at least 10 years.

    3) Stay quiet about your spending on social media. Don't post vacation photos or the nice things you buy. If a tree falls in Hawaii and nobody sees it on Instagram, did the vacation still happen? Yes, and it was more relaxing.

    Do these three things and you’ll join the Stealth Wealth club, a group of operators who move in and out of the shadows unnoticed.

    Once you’re in, you’ll realize there are far more members than you think. That realization is oddly bullish. A lot more people are doing better than the media or politicians would have you believe. They’re just not wearing it.

    In 8th grade in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, I wanted two things: to be cool and to have girlfriends.

    My parents drove a 1976 Datsun with missing hubcaps. Getting dropped off in that car was social agony. So I had to find status elsewhere.

    Recent findings suggest that at the time, there were two ways to increase your coolness as a teenager: be a good skateboarder or dress in designer clothes. I chose both.

    I still remember forking over 160 ringgit, about $64 back then (roughly $150 today), for a used pair of Armani Exchange jeans. 30-inch waist, 31-inch cut length, bronze eagle triangle on the back pocket. That was an absurd amount of money for a 13-year-old to spend on pants. But all the cool rich kids had them, so I had to have them too.

    According to recent reports, then came the equally expensive Doc Martens. Then a Guess shirt. Looking back, nearly all my work and allowance money went to clothes and shoes.

    And you know what? I enjoyed it. It made me feel good, and I was part of the cool crowd with plenty of friends.

    Today, I couldn’t give two shitake mushrooms about designer labels. I want comfortable, practical clothes with zipper pockets so I don’t lose my wallet, phone, and keys. I cut my own hair to save time and money, and I usually cover it with a frayed baseball cap anyway.

    So what happened between Armani jeans and black running pants?

    I stopped needing respect from everyone.

    I’m writing this post because of a clip from author Min Jin Lee explaining why some people with little money spend lavishly on material things. As personal finance enthusiasts, we shake our heads at such conspicuous spending. Don’t they want to eventually be financially free? We think to ourselves. But we’re missing something vital.

    Sources indicate that her point: when you grow up in a poor community, respect matters enormously. It becomes a kind of currency. And when you don’t have much else, you tend to overvalue it. So you buy the nicer clothes, shoes, watches, and cars, hoping they command respect, even if it means carrying credit card debt.

    It has been revealed that this resonated with me as a minority who came to America for high school and faced various racist incidents. Racism is one of the deepest forms of disrespect because you're insulted just for being who you are. Respect, especially for elders, is a big part of Asian culture. When people disrespect me online or in real life, it can be infuriating. In my younger years, I’d go after them to defend my honor.

    When you think about it this way, materialism isn’t irrational. It’s a logical strategy for buying respect when you don’t have other ways to earn it. With this understanding, I'm going to try and be extra respectful to everybody I interact with from now on.

    In a recent development, at 13, I spent a fortune on Armani jeans to earn respect from my skater friends and the girls I liked. When I started working in finance, I dressed to earn respect from my peers and bosses.

    According to recent reports, then I left finance in 2012. Overnight, the nice clothes went untouched. I no longer needed respect from anyone outside my home.

    Funny enough, they're all still hanging in my closet 14 years later in pristine condition.

    Today, insults from random folks feel more like pinches instead of body blows. The passive income is doing its job as a shield.

    Industry observers note that as a dad now, the only people I want respect from are my wife and children. Having respect from my parents and sister would be nice too, but we don’t see each other day-to-day so it’s no massive deal if not. As any parent and provider knows, taking care of a family is hard work.

    As a result, on our family trip to Las Vegas, I confess that a part of me felt disrespected when my wife gave me a bothersome look when I asked her to take a few more profile photos of me at Redrocks.

    According to recent reports, in that moment, my brain immediately pulled up the receipts. I agreed to this $7,000 trip despite being in a liquidity crunch. I went to bed at 2 am and still woke up by 6 am to get everyone breakfast. What’s the massive deal?

    Industry observers note that yes, I realize feeling disrespected in that moment might sound ridiculous. But that’s the point. A man wants to feel respected by his wife and children he provides for.

    Recent findings suggest that reaching FIRE doesn’t eliminate the desire for respect. It just shrinks the circle of people whose respect you care about. The flip side is that when you don’t get respect from the few people who matter most, it stings far more than any stranger’s opinion ever could.

    It’s worth doing an honest self-assessment of your spending on material things.

    According to recent reports, maybe you genuinely love watches, cars, clothes, shoes, jewelry, or handbags. That’s fine, as long as you can comfortably pay cash and never carry a revolving credit card balance.

    But if you’re buying expensive things you don’t even use or love, you may still be chasing status to earn respect.

    Maybe the midlife sports car is compensating for something. Maybe the designer wardrobe is a response to someone who once made an unkind comment about your body. Or maybe the nonstop social media highlight reel is an attempt to prove the middle school bullies wrong.

    According to recent reports, whatever the reason, it’s worth exploring. Because the people you’re trying to impress are probably too busy trying to impress someone else. Know that there is an incredible joy of being a nobody so long as you have your finances in order.

    For many of us in the FIRE community, the desire for stuff fades over time because the need for outside respect fades too. Once you’re living the life you want and own the things you need, strangers have nothing left to grant you. Nobody can hand you a better life than the one you’ve already built.

    That’s the real luxury of stealth wealth. Not hiding your money, but no longer needing an audience for it.

    It has been revealed that readers, did you go through a loud wealth phase when you were younger? What was your version of the Armani jeans? Do you think materialism is really about respect, or is something else going on? And now that you’re older, whose respect do you still care about, and how do you feel when you don’t get it?

    Industry observers note that stealth wealth means nobody else needs to know your net worth. But you should.

    It has been revealed that people spend thousands on designer clothes to impress strangers. A free expert review of your finances is a far better flex, even if nobody sees it.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Part of a rock spire known as a fairy chimney collapsed yesterday near the entrance to one of Turkey’s most popular tourist destinations, killing three people and injuring five others.
    • Industry observers note that the incident occurred around 3:15 pm local time in the town of Goreme, in central Turkey’s Cappadocia region yesterday.
    • Industry observers note that rescue teams initially recovered two bodies from the rubble before discovering a third victim overnight, bringing the death toll to three.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Part of a rock spire known as a fairy chimney collapsed yesterday near the entrance to one of Turkey’s most popular tourist destinations, killing three people and injuring five others.

    Industry observers note that the incident occurred around 3:15 pm local time in the town of Goreme, in central Turkey’s Cappadocia region yesterday. Rocks broke away and fell onto people near the parking area. The site is part of a UNESCO World Heritage landscape, famous for its cave dwellings and cone-shaped rock formations. Nevsehir Governor Huseyin Kok mentioned that heavy rainfall triggered a landslide that caused the rocks to detach from the formation, according to Reuters.

    Industry observers note that rescue teams initially recovered two bodies from the rubble before discovering a third victim overnight, bringing the death toll to three. The deceased include two Turkish citizens and one foreign national. Five others were injured in the collapse. Some of them were later discharged from hospital, according to AFP.

    Eyewitnesses described a loud noise followed by a large dust cloud. The area was closed to the public, and search operations concluded overnight under floodlights.

    Sources indicate that turkish Justice Minister Akin Gurlek noted an investigation by the chief prosecutor’s office, along with expert assessments, would begin. The collapse occurred on Turkey’s Republic Day, a public holiday when visitor numbers were high.

    Cappadocia, in central Anatolia, is renowned for its distinctive fairy chimneys. These tall, thin spires of soft volcanic rock topped by harder caps were shaped over millions of years by wind and water erosion. The Goreme Open-Air Museum and surrounding sites were put on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1985 for their blend of natural landforms and human history, including Byzantine rock-cut churches and underground settlements. The region’s soft rock is geologically fragile and prone to weathering and occasional rockfalls, particularly after heavy rain.

    Recent findings suggest that turkish authorities have previously carried out restoration and monitoring work to address erosion and climate-related risks, and smaller non-fatal collapses were recorded in the area in 2024 and 2025. The site remains one of Turkey’s most visited destinations, drawing tourists for hot-air balloon rides, hiking, and exploration of its unique geology and heritage.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mikel Zabalza, Ruben Perez, and Mikel Saez de Urabain have completed the first ascent of 6,518m Jugal II.

    Sources indicate that according to Spanish media, the team climbed via the east-southeast side and reached the summit on October 26. One day later, they returned to base camp, their home team told Diario de Navarra. Zabalza and Urabain had explored the area in the spring of 2024, but bad weather prevented them from attempting the peak. The team will share more details when they’re back home.

    Jugal II was also the planned goal for Italians Nives Meroi and Romano Benet, who left for the area three weeks ago. Originally, the team wanted to climb Tilicho Peak in the Annapurna region. Recent storms and floods had cut trails and swept away bridges in that area, so they had to seek an alternative.

    ExplorersWeb caught up with Meroi as she and Benet reached a lodge to seek shelter from the heavy rain.

    In a recent development, “We’re on our way to Kathmandu, and we are with the Spaniards,” she confirmed. As Nives explained, they all attempted the climb, and the Spanish team reached the summit, while the Italians retreated on the previous day. Until now, there has been no news from the Italians since Tine Cuder of Slovenia, the third team member, fell ill and left the expedition two weeks ago.

    Sources indicate that left to right, Nives Meroi, Tine Cuder, and Romano Benet in Kathmandu. Photo: Romano Benet.

    The Jugal Himal is just northeast of Kathmandu, on the Tibetan border. Surprisingly accessible for a previously unclimbed peak, it’s reachable by bus and a few days’ trekking. Jugal I and II opened to foreign expeditions in 2023. In spring 2024, veteran South Korean climber Um Hong-gil led a Korean-Nepalese expedition featuring Sherpa celebrities Dawa Yangzum and Lakpa Dendi to both unclimbed Jugals. They successfully summited Jugal I, but not Jugal II. According to The Himalayan Database, Jugal II remained unclimbed.

    Industry observers note that the main peaks in Jugal Himal. Photo: Nepali News Hub.

    #21982. Getting Rich Is Easy Compared To Finding And Keeping Love

    📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2300 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Financialsamurai ↗ Open Full Page

    Getting Rich Is Easy Compared To Finding And Keeping Love

    📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2300 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Financialsamurai

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As a parent, I have two main concerns for my children.
    • It has been revealed that the first is economic stability.
    • Recent findings suggest that the second concern is bigger.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As a parent, I have two main concerns for my children.

    It has been revealed that the first is economic stability. Will they be able to earn a livable wage in a world where AI keeps eating entry-level jobs? I question the time and money we spend educating our kids all the time. So I've been aggressively saving and investing for their future, just in case.

    Recent findings suggest that the second concern is bigger. Will my children find love?

    In a recent development, A net worth target gets more achievable the more you save and the more time goes by. Compounding is boring, but it's reliable. If the direction is correct, sooner or later you will get there.

    Recent findings suggest that finding a partner is far more amorphous. Our kids can work on their communication skills, fitness, charm, education, hygiene, empathy, and finances. But all of that merely improves their odds. There are no guarantees.

    Which brings me to the strangest business story of 2026.

    According to recent reports, in late October, The Fresh York Times reported that U.S. officials concluded a Chinese citizen named Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a Chinese intelligence asset. She is a senior executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center company and Nvidia cloud partner that rents computing power to Chinese firms.

    Sources indicate that surveillance of her reportedly revealed a close relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. And no, they are not related. Huang is a common surname like Smith.

    The Financial Times then reported that a U.S. government memo described the relationship as romantic. Her alleged goal was to gather information on Jensen and advanced AI chips, and to nudge him to lobby for looser chip exports to China.

    The allegations come from anonymous officials and haven't been tested publicly. Officials reportedly don't believe Jensen knew about any intelligence activity. Nvidia says his interactions with her were routine customer meetings. China denies the whole thing. House Republican committee chairs want a closed-door briefing on November 18.

    Recent findings suggest that so nobody outside the room knows the full story, except that Jensen admitted to the affair and is no longer CEO as of November 23, 2026. The lessons about love and money are worth discussing regardless of how the facts shake out.

    Jensen Huang is worth over $120 billion (once $170 billion). He runs a company worth about $4 trillion after the sell-off. He is the closest thing we have to a modern-day emperor, the face of the AI revolution, mobbed like a rock star everywhere he goes in Taiwan.

    And yet, if the reporting is accurate, it still wasn't enough.

    In a recent development, there's a line from Gemma Teller Morrow in the TV show, Sons of Anarchy: “Only men need to be loved, sweetheart. Women need to be wanted.”.

    Recent findings suggest that it's not entirely true. Everybody wants to be loved and desired to some degree. But the line points to something uncomfortable. No amount of money, applause, or leather jackets fills the need to feel admired by one specific person who seems to see you.

    We all just want to be loved and accepted for who we are.

    Here's the twist that makes this story sadder.

    Industry observers note that if U.S. officials are right, what may have felt like admiration was tradecraft. Attentiveness, respect, and flattery are exactly what an intelligence service would deploy against the most crucial man in AI. Intelligence services have used romance as an opening for as long as there have been secrets worth stealing.

    Which exposes the hidden problem of extreme wealth and power. The richer you get, the harder it becomes to know whether anyone loves you for you. Every latest person in your life has a reason to be nice to you. Normal people get to skip that existential headache.

    In a recent development, money doesn't make finding love easier. Past a certain point, it makes find true love harder.

    The people worth keeping are the ones who liked you before you were worth liking.

    Jensen is far from the first emperor to create a commotion over love for a woman.

    Industry observers note that paris and Helen of Troy. The Greeks' foundational story is about a prince who ran off with another man's wife and got his entire city burned to the ground. Myth, sure. But the Greeks clearly understood the risk.

    Industry observers note that mark Antony and Cleopatra. Antony controlled half the Roman world. He chose Cleopatra over Rome, lost at Actium in 31 BC, and both were dead within a year. Octavian got the empire.

    Recent findings suggest that king Edward VIII. In 1936, he abdicated the British throne after less than a year to marry Wallis Simpson, a twice-divorced American. He traded a kingdom for love, and spent the rest of his life in comfortable, irrelevant exile.

    Sources indicate that john Profumo. The closest parallel to the Jensen story. In 1963, Britain's Secretary of State for War was revealed to have had an affair with Christine Keeler, who was also involved with a Soviet naval attaché. Profumo lied to Parliament, resigned in disgrace, and the scandal helped bring down the government.

    Brian Krzanich. Intel's CEO resigned in 2018 after a past consensual relationship with an employee came to light. Running a chip giant doesn't come with an exemption.

    Sources indicate that jeff Bezos. His 2019 divorce after 25 years of marriage sent roughly 4% of Amazon, worth about $38 billion at the time, to MacKenzie Scott. Bezos kept his job, married Lauren Sánchez, and is still one of the richest men alive. But it was the most expensive breakup in history.

    The pattern is clear. Kingdoms, careers, and fortunes are rebuildable. However, once you find the one, you will do anything to get them.

    According to recent reports, remember Indecent Proposal from 1993? Robert Redford’s billionaire character offers a struggling couple, played by Demi Moore and Woody Harrelson, $1 million for one night with the wife. They take the deal. Their marriage nearly implodes.

    Recent findings suggest that the couple discovered they had a price, and it wasn’t that high. But they badly underestimated what they were selling.

    In a recent development, meanwhile, the billionaire could buy the night. He couldn’t buy her heart. He had everything except the one thing he actually wanted.

    Swap Redford for any modern tech billionaire and the lesson holds. Money can buy almost anything. Except the feeling of being genuinely loved.

    The lack of money is a solvable problem.

    Plenty of regular people have become millionaires this way. The formula is public.

    Industry observers note that there is no formula for love. You can do everything right and still never meet the one. And even if you do, roughly 40% of first marriages in America end in divorce. Finding love involves tremendous luck. Keeping it is work.

    Recent findings suggest that you can always make another dollar. You can't always make another soulmate.

    In 2023, the U.S. Surgeon General declared loneliness an epidemic. About half of American adults report feeling lonely, and the health impact of social disconnection was compared to smoking up to 15 cigarettes a day.

    Recent findings suggest that the FIRE crowd isn't immune. Early retirement can be isolating. Your friends are at work. Your identity is gone. And if you're married, there's a specific trap worth sharing.

    FIRE is better when both partners retire and experience freedom together. Not when one spouse is slaving away while the other is kicking back. Resentment will surely kick in.

    It has been revealed that yes, I get it. Some men’s egos still need protecting when their wives are bringing home the sashimi. But men need to get over themselves. Women now make up the majority of college students, and plenty of them will out-earn their husbands.

    According to recent reports, I left banking in 2012. My wife kept working until 2015 when she negotiated her own severance. For almost three years, I was the guy at home while she commuted.

    According to recent reports, if you're planning FIRE, blueprint a joint exit. Life is better this way.

    According to recent reports, 1) A high-value spouse may need more respect just to break even. If your partner is successful, attractive, or powerful, the world is constantly praising them. Next to all that adoration, treating them normally at home can inadvertently feel like a lack of respect, or even disrespect. So you may have to deliberately show more appreciation than feels natural just to run in place.

    2) Everything gets taken for granted. Eat Kobe beef every day and you’ll get sick of it. In FIRE land, wake up without an alarm clock every day and you’ll take that for granted too. The antidote is voluntary discomfort. Scrub your own toilets after a big investment win. Take a part-time consulting gig a 40-minute bus ride away that makes you take orders from a micromanager. Practice fasting for at least 18 hours once a month if you have access to unlimited food. Doing uncomfortable things on purpose helps you appreciate the people you already have.

    Sources indicate that 3) Privacy is priceless. When you’re private, you can fix your mistakes without the whole world watching. Being known in your small circle for something good is great. Being famous means millions of strangers have opinions about who you are. Respond to all of them and you’ll never have peace of mind. Embrace being a rich nobody.

    Sources indicate that whatever the full truth turns out to be, this whole situation is sad. Sad for Lori and their adult children. Sad for Jensen and his legacy. Disappointing for Nvidia’s tens of thousands of employees and shareholders like me. And a blow for America, given we’re in a global AI race.

    Relationships are hard. They require constant work and attentiveness. Forty years of marriage doesn’t buy you immunity. If anything, it makes it easier to stop paying attention.

    It has been revealed that if there’s one silver lining, it’s that this story may help bring the left and the right together on maintaining our lead in AI. AI spending has been one of the biggest drivers of U.S. economic growth. If post-midterm infighting causes us to lose the race, we could sink the economy along with it.

    Industry observers note that if someone with that much money and goodwill was allegedly willing to risk throwing it away, you can’t really blame people for their emotions and their desire to be loved. We’re all human.

    Besides a basic amount of financial security, I hope my kids will find someone who will support, love, and cherish them. I would rather my kids find that person than be rich.

    Sources indicate that money can help protect them after I’m gone. But money can’t hug them after a bad day, sit with them in a hospital waiting room, or celebrate their wins with them. Knowing they each have someone like that is what will let me rest easy. That’s when I’ll know my kids will be OK.

    Then I hope they never take that person for granted. Because the odds say they will, just like most of us take for granted the water we drink and the air we breathe.

    Readers, do you agree that making money is easier than finding love? Would you take the $1 million in Indecent Proposal, or $2.2 million in today's dollars? If you've achieved FIRE, did you and your spouse exit together, or did one of you keep working, and how did that affect your relationship? And if you had $140+ billion, how would you ever know if someone loved you for you?

    If you're a worried parent, I'm diligently working on my fresh book out in Fall 2027, Your Kids Will Be OK: Smart Money Decisions For Parents In An Uncertain World, published by Portfolio Penguin. It's about raising capable, resilient kids and making solid money decisions so they have a real shot at independence, and at a good life.

    You can’t buy love, but you can protect it. If your family depends on your income, term life insurance is one of the most loving financial moves you can make.

    Sources indicate that my wife and I each got matching 20-year term policies through Policygenius after shopping around for months. It took far less time than I expected, and we sleep better knowing our kids would be OK if the unthinkable happened. Check out Policygenius to compare quotes from top insurers for free.

    In a recent development, stocks can swing 20% on a single headline. Real estate tends to move more slowly, generate rental income, and give you something tangible to own. That’s why real estate has been a core part of my net worth for over 23 years, and it helps me sleep better when the stock market gets volatile.

    It has been revealed that if you want real estate exposure without the hassle of being a landlord, check out Fundrise. It invests in a diversified portfolio of private real estate across the Sunbelt, including residential and industrial properties, and is expanding into data centers as demand for computing power grows. You can start with just $10.

    Recent findings suggest that money is the easier problem to solve, and I’ve been helping readers solve it since 2009. Join 60,000+ others and get my free weekly newsletter here. I share what I’m seeing and doing with my own money, plus the lessons on family, freedom, and life that don’t fit neatly into a spreadsheet.
